# A checkout whose git integration was never wired up (the typical "cloned and
# forgot `sesam init`" case) gets a gentle load-time nudge. The integration lives
# in .git/config, which is not cloned, so a fresh clone has none of it even though
# the tracked .sesam files are present. The nudge can be silenced per checkout.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# In the initialized repo the integration is present, so no nudge.
exec sesam status
! stderr 'git-integration is not installed'

# The opt-out marker is a personal, per-checkout decision: gitignored, and it
# lives under .sesam/ so it survives both the stage swap and `sesam clean`.
exec touch .sesam/no-git-integration-warning
exec git check-ignore .sesam/no-git-integration-warning
stdout 'no-git-integration-warning'

# A mutating command commits a stage (a whole-.sesam directory swap); the marker
# is carried across.
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exists .sesam/no-git-integration-warning

# An aggressive clean drops stale plaintext but skips the .sesam/ subtree.
exec sesam clean --aggressive
exists .sesam/no-git-integration-warning

# Simulate a fresh clone: tracked .sesam files come along, the git-config
# integration does not.
exec git clone . theclone

# A command against the clone nudges towards `sesam init`.
exec sesam --sesam-dir theclone status
stderr 'git-integration is not installed'
stderr 'no-git-integration-warning'

# The sentinel opts out per checkout.
exec touch theclone/.sesam/no-git-integration-warning
exec sesam --sesam-dir theclone status
! stderr 'git-integration is not installed'
